subject: Game Theory
title: The Median Voter Theorem
description: Learn The Median Voter Theorem in one minute.

hook.text: Why do candidates in two-party systems sound so similar? They're chasing the same voter.

buildup.text: The median voter theorem says that in majority rule elections, the candidate closest to the median wins.

discovery.text: Both candidates rationally move to the center to capture the median voter, making platforms converge.

twist.text: This model assumes single-issue voting. With multiple issues, polarization can occur despite the theorem.

climax.text: Primary elections push candidates to extremes; general elections push them back to center. A two-stage game.

punchline.text: The center voter picks the winner.

quiz.question: Why do two-party candidates converge to the center?
options: They chase the median voter to win majority
